Class VirtualServerRMI

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsoft.mesos.client.virtualserver.VirtualServerRMI
All Implemented Interfaces:
RmiClientService, Remote
public class VirtualServerRMI extends Object implements RmiClientService
RMI implementation of the server-to-client communication path.

In the RMI client architecture, ServerProxyRMI and VirtualServerRMI own the two opposite directions of the same logical connection:

  • ServerProxyRMI calls the remote server session to send client commands;
  • VirtualServerRMI is exported as a remote callback object so the server can call the client back with updates.

This class is the RMI equivalent of VirtualServerTCP. TCP receives server messages by reading a socket; RMI receives server messages because the server invokes methods on this exported callback object.

The class does not contain UI logic or game logic. It receives already-built ServerMessage objects from the server and delegates routing to MessageRouter, which then calls the appropriate ClientView method.

  • Constructor Details

    • VirtualServerRMI

      public VirtualServerRMI(ClientView clientView) throws RemoteException
      Creates and exports the client callback object used by the RMI server.

      Exporting makes this object reachable from another JVM through Java RMI. After the object is exported, the server can call handleMessage(ServerMessage) and handlePing() remotely.

      Parameters:
      clientView - view contract used to display server updates on the client
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if the callback object cannot be exported

    • VirtualServerRMI

      public VirtualServerRMI(ClientView clientView, boolean exported) throws RemoteException
      Creates the client callback object, optionally exporting it through Java RMI.

      Production code exports the object. Tests can pass false to avoid opening a real RMI export while still exercising the routing behavior.

      Parameters:
      clientView - view contract used to display server updates on the client
      exported - whether this object must be exported through UnicastRemoteObject
      Throws:
      RemoteException - if export is requested and fails

  • Method Details

    • handleMessage

      public void handleMessage(ServerMessage message)
      Receives one server-to-client message through the RMI callback.

      Application messages are routed to the view through MessageRouter. PING is handled separately because it belongs to the connection heartbeat protocol and must produce a PONG response through ServerProxyRMI, not a UI update.

      Specified by:
      handleMessage in interface RmiClientService
      Parameters:
      message - message sent by the remote server

    • attachServerProxy

      public void attachServerProxy(ServerProxyRMI serverProxy)
      Connects this server-to-client callback with the matching client-to-server proxy.

      The reference is needed only for heartbeat handling: when the server sends a PING callback, this object answers by asking ServerProxyRMI to send PONG to the remote server session.

      Parameters:
      serverProxy - proxy connected to the same RMI server session

    • handlePing

      public void handlePing()
      Handles the RMI heartbeat request sent by the server.

      PING is not shown to the user. The callback answers by using the attached ServerProxyRMI to send PONG on the client-to-server direction of the RMI session.

      Specified by:
      handlePing in interface RmiClientService
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the callback has not yet been attached to its proxy

    • close

      public void close() throws NoSuchObjectException
      Releases the RMI callback object exported for this client.

      Only exported instances must be unexported. Test instances created with exported == false do not own an RMI export and therefore have nothing to release.

      Throws:
      NoSuchObjectException - if RMI cannot find this exported object during unexport
